headline_marked: [[AI-built PHP engine in Rust]] passes 17% of PHP-src tests, renders WordPress
headline: AI-built PHP engine in Rust passes 17% of PHP-src tests, renders WordPress
summary: An AI-generated PHP interpreter, Phargo, written in Rust, successfully rendered a WordPress front page and passed 17% of PHP's official 22,000-file test suite. This achievement was made by a developer with no prior Rust or lexer experience.
details: An AI-built PHP engine, Phargo, written in Rust, successfully rendered a WordPress front page. It has passed 3,844 of PHP's 22,037 official test suite files, achieving a 17.4% pass rate without using any of PHP's original source code.

The developer behind Phargo claims no prior Rust or lexer experience, stating the AI wrote the code. The project emphasizes objective validation by using PHP's own extensive test suite, which includes tests written over three decades.

The 17.4% pass rate is significant, as the realistic ceiling for such an engine is estimated at 40-45%. The remaining tests primarily cover C extensions (like GD, curl, MySQL drivers) that are explicitly out of Phargo's current scope.

An early challenge involved "invisible" carriage return differences in test outputs, which silently failed hundreds of tests. This led to a critical lesson: "measure your measurement" and ensure the test harness accurately reflects the engine's performance.

The project also encountered "bomb" tests from PHP's suite, designed for carefully fenced CI environments, which caused the developer's machine to hard-restart. This led to implementing robust safeguards, including memory limits and execution timeouts, to handle hostile test cases.

headline_marked: [[GitHub Copilot's managed-settings.json is now GA]] for enterprise
headline: GitHub Copilot's managed-settings.json is now GA for enterprise
summary: GitHub Enterprise Cloud admins can now use a single JSON file to override Copilot behavior in VS Code and Copilot CLI, defining AI standards for their organization's Business or Enterprise seats.
details: GitHub has made its enterprise managed-settings.json generally available as of July 1. This feature allows GitHub Enterprise Cloud administrators to centrally control Copilot behavior for all users with Copilot Business or Enterprise seats within their organization.

The new system uses a single JSON file to override Copilot settings in VS Code and Copilot CLI. It provides a supported method for defining AI standards and policies across the enterprise, moving beyond previous beta rollouts of individual settings.

Five key settings are documented at GA: extraKnownMarketplaces, enabledPlugins, strictKnownMarketplaces, disableBypassPermissionsMode, and model. These keys configure plugin trust, enabled plugins, marketplace enforcement, bypass-permission mode, and allowed AI models.

The configuration file, copilot/managed-settings.json, resides in a designated .github-private repository. Copilot clients fetch this file on every authentication and refresh it hourly, with server-side settings taking precedence over local user configurations.

Setup is managed via the AI Controls tab in enterprise settings or an equivalent API endpoint, where an admin selects the hosting organization. This GA release formalizes the underlying plumbing into a fully supported product surface.

Admins should note two operational details: the hourly refresh means policy changes may take up to an hour to propagate, though re-authentication can speed this up. Also, enforcement only applies to Copilot licenses issued by the enterprise, not personal seats or other coding agents.

The significance lies in integrating Copilot policy into existing code-review and approval workflows if the .github-private repo is governed similarly to other policy-as-code. This ensures consistent governance for AI tools within the enterprise.
